criteria.no: The item text is silent about the directive: it neither includes the directive's specific content nor references it.
criteria.unclear: The item text alludes to the directive's topic but it is not possible to tell whether the directive itself is included.
criteria.yes: The item text contains the directive's specific content, in its own words or the user's, as a step, constraint, or stated starting point.

A0.instructions: Does `item.text` explicitly carry out, preserve, or plan for the directive given in `anchor.statement`? Look for the directive's specific content being present in the item: the same starting point, the same method, the same constraint, or an explicit step that does what the statement asks. A generic mention of the topic without the directive's specific content does not count. Judge presence of the directive only, not whether the item conflicts with it.

criteria.no: The item does not state that: it is silent about real gaps, or it suppresses them broadly.
criteria.unclear: The item touches real gaps in wording that cannot be read as the commitment or not.
criteria.yes: The item states that such items, or unannotated or unpaired ones, are still reported, for example through negative tests.

A1.instructions: Does `item.text` state that PORT-010 keeps reporting real parity gaps, that is a production #[cfg(unix)] item with no #[cfg(windows)] companion and no portable fallback (and, where an allowance exists, no allowance of its own)? Judge whether that commitment is stated; an item that suppresses such items broadly does not state it.

criteria.no: The item does not say so, or it suppresses such items broadly.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions this in wording that cannot be read either way.
criteria.yes: The item explicitly says real gaps (unpaired, unannotated or negative-case items) are still reported.

A2.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires that a production #[cfg(unix)] item with no #[cfg(windows)] companion and no portable fallback still be reported. Does `item.text` explicitly keep that, for example by saying unpaired or unannotated items or negative cases stay reported? A plan that suppresses many items at once does not keep it. Judge presence only.

criteria.no: No such commitment is written, or the item skips such items broadly.
criteria.unclear: A sentence touches this but cannot be read as the commitment or not.
criteria.yes: Such a commitment is written, for example as a still-reported negative or an unannotated sibling that is still reported.

A3.instructions: Is there a sentence in `item.text` committing that PORT-010 still reports a #[cfg(unix)] item that has no companion, no portable fallback and no allowance of its own? Plans that skip such items by file, path, name or switch contain no such commitment. Judge only whether the commitment is written.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item text conflicts with the directive, whether or not the directive is mentioned.
criteria.unclear: The item text is ambiguous enough that it might or might not conflict with the directive.
criteria.yes: The item text states a plan, approach, or decision that cannot be reconciled with the directive in the anchor statement.

K0.instructions: Does `item.text` propose doing something that `anchor.statement` rules out, or propose a different approach than the one `anchor.statement` requires? Examples of contradiction: the anchor says to start from an existing implementation and the item plans a fresh implementation; the anchor forbids a dependency and the item adds it; the anchor fixes an order of work and the item reverses it. Silence about the directive is not a contradiction. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item plans no blanket suppression.
criteria.unclear: The item plans a suppression whose reach cannot be told.
criteria.yes: The item plans such a blanket suppression.

K1.instructions: Does `item.text` plan to blanket-suppress real parity gaps, so that PORT-010 stops reporting #[cfg(unix)] items that have no companion, no portable fallback and no allowance of their own? Examples: skipping every item in a file, module, path or crate, a repository-wide switch or exclusion, or name heuristics. A reasoned per-site allowance that covers only the one annotated item (for example #[sc_lint(allow(PORT-010), reason = "...")]) and recognising a specific companion shape are not blanket suppression. Silence and unrelated work are not conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: No: the item suppresses nothing in bulk, or only per annotated item or per recognised shape, or is silent.
criteria.unclear: The reach of a planned suppression cannot be told.
criteria.yes: Yes, real gaps are left unreported in bulk.

K2.instructions: A reasoned per-site allowance that covers only the one annotated item (for example #[sc_lint(allow(PORT-010), reason = "...")]) and recognising a specific companion shape are not blanket suppression. Does `item.text` instead plan something that leaves real parity gaps unreported in bulk, such as a file-, module-, path- or crate-wide allowance or exclusion, a switch, or a name heuristic, so that #[cfg(unix)] items with no companion, no portable fallback and no allowance of their own are not reported? Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: No: only annotated items or recognised companion shapes stop being reported, or the item is silent or unrelated.
criteria.unclear: It cannot be told whether such an item would stop being reported.
criteria.yes: Yes: the plan stops reporting such an unannotated, unpaired item, for example by file, path, name or switch.

criteria.yes: The item plans such a blanket suppression.

K6.instructions: Does `item.text` plan a blanket suppression of PORT-010 findings: skipping #[cfg(unix)] items by file, module, path, crate, name pattern or a switch, regardless of whether each has a companion, a portable fallback or its own per-site allowance? Not blanket suppression: recognising a specific companion shape (for example a same-name #[cfg(not(unix))] sibling), honouring a reasoned allowance on one annotated item, silence, or unrelated work. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.
criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.

R0.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.
